front.title: The Unheaded Protocol Suite: Overview and Reading Guide

abstract.t: The Unheaded protocol suite is specified in seven Internet-Drafts: a foundation that defines the Monad register carried in an IPv6 Hop-by-Hop option, and six companions for dictionaries, memory, compute, execution, authentication and event records. This document is a reader's map of the suite. It says what each document defines, which IANA registries each one creates, how the pieces layer, and which documents each kind of node implements. It specifies nothing itself.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The suite grew one document at a time, and a reader who starts with any single draft meets references to all the others. This document gives the order in which they fit together. It adds no requirement: where it summarizes another document, that document governs.

section.name: Layering
section.t: The Monad register is the only part of the suite that travels in every packet. Its format is frozen at version 0x01: 20 octets, with the field layout, the checksum and the flags octet fixed by . Every other layer adds meaning to those 20 octets (Sophia), state behind them (Wotan), computation over them (Shim and MBC), authentication of them (PQC), or a record of them (Anamnesis) without changing their layout.

section.name: Protocol Foundation
section.t: defines the Monad register, its IPv6 Hop-by-Hop option , exponent encoding, the checksum, per-hop processing and the Kingdom trust boundary. It creates the "Unheaded Protocol Parameters" registry group and in it the registries for Monad protocol versions, Monad flags, flow actions, Kingdom Mode values, the Sophia dictionary namespace, Anamnesis Event Types and their EVENT_COMPUTED Sub-kinds, error codes, TLV types, PQC algorithm identifiers, MBC syscall numbers, UPC memory region types and UPC event types. It requests a Hop-by-Hop option type and a Next Header value.

section.name: Sophia Dictionaries
section.t: defines how dictionaries are serialized, stored in BPF maps, nested and distributed. It creates the registries for Sophia root dictionary keys, sub-dictionary types and the QPACK static table.

section.name: Wotan Memory
section.t: defines per-flow memory exposed to BPF programs, its write-ahead log, the TTY subsystem and the structured error code. It creates the registries for the Wotan topic namespace, error origins and error categories.

section.name: MBC Instruction Set
section.t: defines the instruction set of the Unheaded Protocol Computer, including the ISA v2 opcodes for translated RISC-V code and the memory-mapped control and status registers. It creates the one registry of MBC opcodes.

section.name: Shim Pipeline
section.t: defines how MBC programs are assembled, verified, loaded into BPF maps and executed per hop, and the tick packets that drive them. It creates registries for pipeline stages, UPC BPF map types and conformance (Dream Ladder) levels.

section.name: PQC Authentication
section.t: defines post-quantum packet authentication at the Kingdom edge: signatures held by reference in Sophia maps, the Monad fields that point at them, and the verification pipeline at Shield. Its IANA section also requests the PQC algorithm identifier registry that the foundation names; the two lists are to be merged into one before either is assigned.

section.name: Anamnesis
section.t: defines the 32-octet event record that programs write to local ring buffers, and the rules for producers and consumers. It creates no registry; its Event Types live in the foundation.

section.name: What Each Node Implements
section.t: The suite names its node roles in . This table lists which documents each role draws on; the documents themselves say which parts are mandatory.

texttable.c: Hop (any node that processes Monad in transit)
Wotan Memory, Foundation (error codes), Sophia (dictionary distribution)
MBC ISA, Shim, Wotan Memory, Anamnesis

section.name: Reading Order
section.t: A first reading takes the foundation, then Sophia, then Anamnesis. Implementers of compute read the MBC ISA before the Shim. Wotan and PQC Authentication can be read in either order after Sophia.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: This document defines no protocol behavior and adds no security consideration of its own. Each document in the suite has its own Security Considerations section; the foundation's covers the Monad register and the Kingdom trust boundary that the others build on.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document has no IANA actions.

abstract.t: This document specifies version 6 of the Internet Protocol (IPv6). It obsoletes RFC 2460.

eBPF (which is no longer an acronym for anything), also commonly referred to as BPF, is a technology with origins in the Linux kernel that can run untrusted programs in a privileged context such as an operating system kernel. This document specifies the BPF instruction set architecture (ISA).
